stewards.name: Tempo Labs
stewards.role: Co-author of the core (three of five authors); sole author of both intent drafts, the MCP transport draft and the three Tempo method drafts; co-author of the discovery draft (with Merit Systems) and the stripe method drafts (with Stripe); runs mpp.dev; since 2026-11-19 it also runs an x402 facilitator that takes USDC on Base and pays sellers in OUSD on Tempo.

stewards.name: Stripe
stewards.role: Co-author of the core (two authors) and of the stripe methods; settles MPP payments in its platform.

stewards.name: Rail authors
stewards.role: Visa (card), Lightspark (lightning), Circle (usdc), Coinbase, MegaETH Labs and Monad Foundation (evm charge), OKG (evm session), Solana Foundation, Stellar Development Foundation, Hedera, Near One and Ripple maintain their methods.

implementers.name: Stripe (MPP acceptance with deposit addresses and SPTs)
implementers.role: Accepts MPP payments in stablecoins (USDC.e on Tempo, USDC on Solana) and in cards, Klarna and Affirm through SPTs, and runs streaming payments over MPP sessions on Tempo; stablecoin payments are open to businesses in every US state except New York; docs labeled Frontier.

implementers.name: Visa (mpp-card SDK)
implementers.role: Card method author and design partner for cards.

implementers.name: Lightspark
implementers.role: Lightning method author. mpp.dev names @buildonspark/lightning-mpp-sdk (0.1.4, 2026-03-18), whose npm maintainers include Lightspark addresses, as the lightning implementation; session support is listed as coming soon (2026-10-21).

implementers.name: Cloudflare Agents SDK
implementers.role: Documents MPP and uses mppx in guides.

implementers.name: Browserbase, PostalForm, Prospect Butcher Co., Stripe Climate, Parallel Web Systems
implementers.role: Named by Stripe at launch as MPP users.

implementers.name: Alchemy, Dune Analytics, Merit Systems
implementers.role: Named by Tempo in the launch directory.

implementers.name: Merit Systems (MPPscan)
implementers.role: Runs the MPP explorer and co-authored the discovery draft.

implementers.name: Tempo Wallet MACH
implementers.role: On-chain credit that an agent spends over MPP at approved merchants on Tempo, within limits the user approves: 1 USD buys 1 MACH through Coinflow, and MACH does not expire and cannot be sent to another personal wallet, redeemed for cash, swapped or bridged. On 2026-10-21, 19 directory listings carried the supportsMACH flag, and 22 on 2026-11-21.

implementers.name: Lightning Labs Aperture
implementers.role: L402 reverse proxy that, by Lightning Labs' account, has also served MPP's Payment scheme with Lightning charge and session intents since v0.5.0 (2026-03-25), with one 402 that can carry both an L402 and a Payment challenge; v0.6.0 (2026-11-05) brought that implementation up to the spec. MPP support is opt-in and needs SQL storage, and the MPP repositories do not list Aperture.

implementers.name: Tempo Wallet MPP Credits (legacy)
implementers.role: Card-funded credits for MPP services, announced 2026-06-17. On 2026-10-21 Tempo Wallet calls them legacy and keeps them separate from MACH; buying MACH does not convert them.

implementers.name: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore payments (buyer side)
implementers.role: Pays MPP charge challenges for agents since its general availability on 2026-08-18 (AWS's notice says Machine Payment Protocol): it checks a session budget, signs with a Coinbase CDP or Stripe (Privy) wallet and returns the Authorization value, for the evm, tempo and solana methods. Charge intent only, one challenge per call.

implementers.name: AWS WAF AI traffic monetization
implementers.role: Answers AI bots and agents with x402 at the edge since 2026-06-15, settled through Coinbase's facilitator. AWS said MPP support was coming soon; the WAF developer guide read on 2026-11-21 still names only x402.

sdks.name: mppx
sdks.note: TypeScript SDK by wevm, MIT, and the reference SDK named in the shared AGENTS.md of mpp-specs; server, client, CLI, proxy; serves x402 exact offers since 0.6.29 (2026-06-02) and has dual MPP and x402 framework wrappers since 0.9.0 (2026-08-27). Since 0.16.0 (2026-10-28) it carries the per-route identity framework, with Poppy (0.19.1) and ERC-8004 (0.20.0) providers since 2026-11-16, and since 0.18.0 its Tempo server methods refuse to start in production without an explicitly configured store. 0.20.0 (2026-11-16) and 0.21.0 (2026-11-19) fixed payment-boundary flaws without an advisory and both need migration; 0.21.1 adds tempoX402() for Tempo's x402 facilitator. Version 0.21.1 of 2026-11-19, latest as of 2026-11-21.

sdks.name: pympp
sdks.note: Python SDK by tempoxyz. Version 0.26.0 of 2026-11-19, latest as of 2026-11-21 (0.22.0 on 2026-11-14; no 0.23.0 was published). 0.24.0 (2026-11-16) added identity primitives and a Tempo ID provider, 0.25.0 x402 Sign-In with X, and 0.26.0 Zone payments, x402_extra and facilitator_pay_to().

sdks.name: mpp
sdks.note: Rust SDK (tempoxyz/mpp-rs). Version 0.21.0 of 2026-11-16, latest as of 2026-11-21 (0.20.0 on 2026-11-14): Tempo Wallet's MACH funding link, identity providers, and a replay fix in TempoChargeMethod::new with no advisory.

sdks.name: github.com/tempoxyz/mpp-go
sdks.note: Go SDK. Version v0.9.1 of 2026-11-16, latest as of 2026-11-21 (v0.9.0 on 2026-11-14): prevents duplicate MCP payments and adds a database/sql replay store.

sdks.name: mpp-rb
sdks.note: Ruby SDK in stripe/mpp-rb. Version 0.1.10 of 2026-10-26, latest as of 2026-11-21.

sdks.name: mpp-card
sdks.note: Visa card method SDK; proprietary license; no TAP signing code. Version as of 2026-11-21, unchanged since 2026-03-18.

sdks.name: @solana/mpp
sdks.note: Solana method. Version as of 2026-11-21, unchanged since 2026-07-13.

sdks.name: @stellar/mpp
sdks.note: Stellar method. Version as of 2026-11-21, unchanged since 2026-07-02.

sdks.name: @buildonspark/lightning-mpp-sdk
sdks.note: Lightning method SDK that extends mppx, in the Spark organization's repository (MIT), with Lightspark addresses among its npm maintainers; mpp.dev's lightning page lists session support as coming soon. Version 0.1.4 of 2026-03-18, latest as of 2026-11-21.

metrics.caveat: The indexer's own definition: MPPscan publishes no counting method and does not say whether test or wash payments are excluded, while Visa and Artemis exclude identified wash and test activity from their adjusted totals. A Merit Systems page dated 2026-06-24 shows the same live figures, so they are not June values. Read on 2026-11-14, the newest indexed transaction dated from 2026-11-11T17:14:56Z and the 1-day window read 0, so the indexer appears to have stopped then. The count was 4,250,945 on 2026-10-21. Read again on 2026-11-21 the value had not changed, because the indexer had added nothing since 2026-11-11.

About 0.09 USD per transaction on average; indexed data ends on 2026-11-11. The total was 437,665 USD on 2026-10-21. Read again on 2026-11-21 the value had not changed, because the indexer had added nothing since 2026-11-11.

metrics.metric: MPPscan unique senders and recipients, all time
metrics.caveat: Addresses, not agents or businesses; indexed data ends on 2026-11-11. The figures were 224,823 / 6,138 on 2026-10-21. Read again on 2026-11-21 the value had not changed, because the indexer had added nothing since 2026-11-11.

Not comparable with the earlier reading: indexed data ends on 2026-11-11, so the window holds about 26.6 indexed days. Per indexed day that is about 20,100 transactions and 327 USD, about 1.6 cents each. On 2026-10-21 the full window read 785,833 transactions and 8,620 USD, about 26,200 and 287 USD a day at about 1.1 cents each. Re-read on 2026-11-21 the window showed 417,898 transactions and 7,086 USD over only about 20 indexed days; the fall reflects the stalled indexer, not lower use.

metrics.definition: Rolling 7-day window shown by default on the homepage.
metrics.caveat: Holds only about 3.6 indexed days because indexed data ends on 2026-11-11, so do not read a decline into it. On 2026-10-21 the window read 120,727 transactions and 1,560 USD. Do not read the homepage numbers as all-time totals. Re-read on 2026-11-21 the window read 0, because nothing had been indexed since 2026-11-11.

metrics.definition: Listings in mpp.dev/api/services; 139 accept tempo, 10 stripe, 1 evm; 22 carry the supportsMACH flag.
metrics.caveat: A listing, not usage. The directory had 139 listings on 2026-11-14 and 138 on 2026-10-21.

metrics.definition: Adjusted totals from the mid-March 2026 launch to 2026-04-21, excluding identified wash and test activity (Visa and Artemis, on Artemis on-chain data).
metrics.caveat: About 0.22 USD each. Visa's summary page was last updated 2026-07-14; Forkast (2026-07-20) repeats the figures.

metrics.definition: Stars on the two main repositories.

costs.value: None defined in any MPP spec; costs come from the rail
costs.caveat: Rail and processor fees still apply.

costs.value: Paid in USD TIP-20 stablecoins through the Fee AMM; the base fee for a 50,000-gas transfer is capped at about 0.0006 USD, with a quiet-period floor near 0.00003 USD, and optional priority fees come on top
costs.whoPays: Client by default; server when feePayer is true for charge, open and topUp; server always for settle and close
costs.caveat: Depends on Tempo base fee parameters; fees go to the proposing validator.

costs.value: Open on an existing reserve balance 72.1 percent less gas (294,425 versus 1,055,229); settle to a new payee balance 79.4 percent more (559,871)
costs.caveat: Up to 72 percent is the best case for one operation, not an average.

costs.value: Stripe pays customers' Tempo network fees
costs.caveat: Needs mppx 0.9.2 or later, live mode and a Tempo deposit address on the same account; not with Connect.

costs.value: 0.50 USD for SPT card payments; 0.01 USDC for stablecoin payments
1.5 percent of the transaction amount in USD, with conversion to fiat, wallet and AML screening, fraud prevention and gas sponsorship included (Stripe's US pricing page)
costs.caveat: Stripe's machine payments docs take MPP stablecoin payments through the Stablecoins and Crypto payment method, but no Stripe page names a rate for MPP or says whether this one applies to MPP charges. The 0.8 percent promotional stablecoin rate on the same page belongs to Link. The press reported the 1.5 percent in December 2025.

costs.value: 0.15 USD per SPT issued (Stripe's US pricing page)
costs.whoPays: Not stated; Stripe prices it per SPT issued, and the page's Learn more link opens the agent-side SPT docs
costs.caveat: Listed since at least 2026-04-23, the first archived copy that shows it. The page does not name the party billed or say how the price applies to SPTs used through MPP; the SPT docs, labeled Public preview, show no price.

costs.whoPays: No MPP-specific fee published; standard card acceptance costs (interchange, scheme and acquirer fees) are assumed to apply
costs.caveat: Evidence of absence: Visa's 2026-03-18 announcement and the card method spec name no price, and a secondary review of Visa Intelligent Commerce (Nevermined, 2026-08-19) reports no published agent-specific interchange or token fee. The atlas treats these payments as standard tokenized card-not-present economics until the networks publish otherwise. Stripe's SPT price belongs to the stripe method, not to this card method.
